threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still go to Broadway Market on Saturdays like it’s a novelty, rather than just your go-to for overpriced avocado toast.
Last night, the 133 stopped to let on a guy with a full saxophone. He played a solo the whole way to Camberwell, we were all just vibing.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted a guy practicing opera in the park while his dog chased pigeons. That’s Neukölln for you—chaos meets creativity.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find the spontaneous street concerts on random corners, where locals just whip out instruments and jam in the sunset.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they know to avoid BART during rush hour after a smoke scare—no one who's just working here would bother.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a street performer on the 49 bus today. He used the handrail like a mic stand, belting out oldies. Only in SF do you get a concert with your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists don’t realize that the best tapas spots aren’t on Carrer Gran de Gràcia but tucked away on tiny side streets. Big difference.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their tendency to ask for 'una tapa de patatas bravas' at every bar, instead of just 'bravas'.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask where to find 'real' coffee instead of just knowing it’s around every corner from the 24-hour bagel shop.
Last night on the 35, a guy dressed as a banana argued with the driver about the legitimacy of fruit-themed disguises. We laughed all the way to Norwood.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy in a suit arguing with a dog over a tram seat. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a kebab shop open at 3 AM serving more locals than tourists, complete with a terrace full of art students chatting about philosophy.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell someone’s a local if they know to avoid the BART platform at Civic Center on nights when the train breaks down—like clockwork.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in full business attire casually reading a novel on the 19 bus while a street musician played Mozart outside. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the Mercat de l'Abaceria is just a market for souvenirs. It’s actually where locals grab the freshest produce and gossip at dawn.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the local bus maps—most locals know that the best way is just to follow the crowd.
